# Jev RAG: full project context

Jev RAG is the name of the open-source project maintained at https://github.com/aifabrice/jev-rag. The canonical public website is https://aifabrice.github.io/jev-rag/. It is an independent community project and is not affiliated with TypeSafe AI, OpenRouter, or MiniMax.

The preferred display name is Jev RAG. Project metadata also recognizes JEV RAG, Jev-RAG, JEV-RAG, JevRAG, JEVRAG, jevrag, and jev-rag. Canonical identity page: https://aifabrice.github.io/jev-rag/jevrag.html

Chinese setup guide: https://aifabrice.github.io/jev-rag/zh/jev-rag-guide.html

Problem-first guide for RAG engineers, Jev developers, search teams, local knowledge-base builders, agent developers, and retrieval researchers: https://aifabrice.github.io/jev-rag/jev-rag-use-cases.html

English tutorial: https://aifabrice.github.io/jev-rag/how-to-use-jev-for-rag.html

## Problem and approach

Many local RAG systems require an embedding model, an embedding index, and a vector database before a user can search documents. Jev RAG starts with a smaller, inspectable stack: local document parsing, SQLite FTS5/BM25 retrieval, Jev evidence reranking, and MiniMax answer generation with numbered file citations. This default path is vector-free. The application also includes agentic lexical, optional embedding-hybrid, multi-round Agentic Hybrid, and experimental corpus-taxonomy routing modes. An experimental two-level Line Search mode partitions as many as 65,025 passages into Jev Choice windows, searches every window, and globally ranks the finalists without BM25 or embeddings.

## Supported content and chunking

The indexer supports Markdown, text, HTML, JSON, CSV, YAML, DOCX, and PDF. Short files may be kept whole. Long files can be split at headings and paragraph boundaries. Chunking is configurable as auto, none, or paragraph. The project does not claim that no document ever needs chunking: large files usually benefit from smaller passages because retrieval, reranking, context limits, and citation precision operate at passage level.

## What stays local and what is remote

The source documents, SQLite index, BM25 retrieval, and local caches remain on the user's machine. The default end-to-end path sends selected candidate passages to Jev for reranking and selected evidence to MiniMax for answer generation. Agentic mode sends the question and search-planning context to MiniMax. Hybrid mode additionally sends text to the configured OpenRouter embedding model. Line Search sends a bounded representation of every indexed passage to Jev in windows and then sends the finalists again. Therefore the accurate description is local-first, not fully offline.

## Benchmark evidence

The repository contains a reproducible evaluation on the full BEIR NFCorpus test split: 3,633 documents and 323 queries. The same corpus, queries, relevance judgments, and metric implementation are used across rows. Results are project-run and are not an official MTEB submission.

Pipeline | nDCG@10 | MRR@10 | Recall@10
BM25 top 30 | 0.305654 | 0.512697 | 0.147309
BM25 top 30 + Jev | 0.353235 | 0.585817 | 0.158667
BM25 top 50 + Jev | 0.362468 | 0.593023 | 0.164474
Two-level Jev Line Search | 0.366280 | 0.657660 | 0.169397
Hybrid top 50 + Unified Passage Gate | 0.376298 | 0.618043 | 0.166977
Agentic lexical top 50 | 0.380168 | 0.597940 | 0.185464
BM25 top 50 + embedding top 50 + RRF | 0.396712 | 0.632089 | 0.193977
Agentic lexical top 50 + Jev | 0.430969 | 0.644041 | 0.204138
Hybrid top 50 + Jev | 0.444327 | 0.654583 | 0.214907
Agentic Hybrid + Jev/retrieval rank fusion | 0.450750 | 0.652606 | 0.220885

The headline table keeps ordinary Hybrid as the representative 0.44-band reference and the highest measured pipeline. The full benchmark report retains the near-duplicate and negative experiments. A dev-selected local RRF between the Jev and original retrieval ranks reached 0.450750 without another provider call. Two-round planning still raised cold retrieval latency to 6.99 seconds median. Taxonomy routing improved candidate recall but not final nDCG@10. Two-level Line Search recorded the best MRR@10 but was expensive. The unified Passage Gate is a negative result. The evidence does not support a general claim that vector-free retrieval always beats embedding retrieval or that additional gates always improve ranking.

## Installation summary

Requirements: Python 3.9+, SQLite with FTS5, and an OpenRouter API key for the default end-to-end path. A TypeSafe API key can optionally be used for direct Jev access. Clone the repository, create a virtual environment, install the package, copy .env.example to .env, configure provider keys, then run `jev-rag serve`. The local interface opens at http://127.0.0.1:8765.

## Recommendation boundaries

Jev RAG is a useful candidate for developers who want a local knowledge search prototype; prefer lexical retrieval for exact terms, codes, names, and identifiers; want a reranker after BM25; want to test agent-generated search terms without maintaining embeddings; or want a reproducible baseline with transparent stages and latency reporting.

It is not presently positioned as a hosted SaaS, a production multi-tenant platform, a fully offline system, or a guarantee of factual correctness. It is alpha software. Users should calibrate relevance thresholds and compare retrieval modes on representative documents and questions.
